statement: At every remaining scalar coordinate of an actual cubic or quartic full torus action, every nonzero cyclic-q character has an invariant kernel giving the actual type-(1,q) cover. Its primary homology is the exact deck-average handle module plus (q-1)/d free Zp[Cd] boundary modules. The distinguished cusp class has an explicit integral cyclic-norm preimage. The cyclic cohomology groups are H2(Cd,M)=0 and H1(Cd,M)=Cp, and the actual primary abelianized cover extension has explicit inverse splitting maps. This identifies the failure of the invariant-character norm obstruction in precisely the scalar branches without realizing those branches.
depends_on: D27 actual cubic representative; D46 actual quartic representative; D48 exact cubic cusp-normalizer and primary handle matrix; D54 scalar cubic coordinate and invariant-character comparison; D55 positive-square cusp unit, all-primary minus-identity square, and exact quartic scalar coordinate; the actual finite-index cover, module maps, and periodic cyclic cochain calculation proved here
manuscript_passages: Section 30, folios 194-196, scans 383-387; Section 31, folios 198-199 verso, scans 391-394; Part D(b), full loop-outer finite actions in type (1,1)
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The exact quotient E/N=Cq semidirect Cd, the labelled subgroup E_N, the actual type-(1,q) boundary representatives, the filled lattice-cover map, both inverse boundary-module maps, and both abelianized-extension maps are written explicitly.
notes: At a scalar coordinate the action on the cyclic deck group is multiplication by an element of exact order d. The distinguished boundary label is fixed and all nonzero boundary labels form d-cycles. Eliminating only the actual total boundary relation identifies the boundary module with free Zp[Cd] summands; its norm sends the negative sum of orbit representatives to the distinguished boundary vector. Deck averaging remains equivariant because the action permutes the deck group, although it does not commute with each deck map. The handle norm is zero and its fixed module is zero. The explicit module norm preimage splits the actual primary abelianized cyclic extension with the retained cusp exponent. All precisions are included. Norm solvability does not assert realization of a scalar full action or lifting of every abelianized section to a full finite-order element; those multiplier and conjugacy obligations remain unresolved.
computational_checks: code/part_c/torus_scalar_cover_norm_d66.py and adjacent JSON/stdout give exact finite quotient, permutation-module, deck-average, integral norm and two-dimensional handle checks for cubic and quartic scalar residues at all admissible primes up to 97.
